models_evaluated: Faster R-CNN rib fracture detection model

links.outcome: Prospective performance of passive (silent) AI on live ED chest radiographs versus radiologist reports
links.effect: Passive deployment on 23,251 radiographs: sensitivity 74.5%, specificity 93.3%, PPV 24.2%, NPV 99.2%; 14-day GPU outage exposed infrastructure fragility; median inference 10.6 s vs 3.3 h.
links.quote: AI operated passively, without influencing clinical decision-making.

links.outcome: Error rates of AI rib fracture detection relevant to stand-alone diagnostic use
links.effect: Sensitivity 74.5%, PPV 24.2%; false-positive and false-negative rates indicate AI should be a supportive screening tool, not stand-alone diagnostic.
links.quote: Although the system showed high negative predictive value, the observed false-positive and false-negative rates indicate that it should be considered a supportive screening tool rather than a stand-alone diagnostic solution or a replacement for clinical judgment.

unlisted_practices: Infrastructure resilience planning for GPU outage
Analysis of imaging demand patterns for capacity planning

screen.reason: Prospective observational study evaluating the diagnostic accuracy, processing speed, and technical feasibility of an AI model deployed passively (silent mode) in an emergency department workflow without testing a specific organizational safeguard or comparative deployment practice.
